preamble: Secondary (Adaptive/Hyperfiltration) FSGS  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  KDIGO 2021 Glomerular Disease Guidelines / Obesity-Related Glomerulopathy Consensus  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: In obesity-related FSGS: is BMI still ≥35 or has weight loss achieved <10% from peak weight?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — insufficient weight reduction; obesity drive of hyperfiltration persists; proteinuria will not remit without sustained weight loss

questions.question: In reduced-nephron-mass FSGS: is the solitary/reduced kidney experiencing progressive CKD without compensatory treatment?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — nephron mass cannot be restored; lifelong RAS blockade and proteinuria minimization are the primary interventions

questions.question: In sickle cell or reflux nephropathy FSGS: is the underlying disease inadequately controlled (active sickling crises or ongoing reflux without surgical correction)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — underlying driver uncontrolled; FSGS progression will continue without disease-specific management

questions.question: Is proteinuria >1 g/day (PCR >1.0 mg/mg) despite ≥3 months of maximum-tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB dose?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — inadequate proteinuria response to RAS blockade; add SGLT-2 inhibitor; reassess cause control; consider sparsentan

questions.question: Has proteinuria increased ≥50% from baseline over ≥6 months despite optimized RAS blockade?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — worsening proteinuria trajectory on therapy; underlying hyperfiltration burden increasing; escalate cause control urgently

questions.question: Is eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 3b) or declining below estimated nephron reserve for the underlying structural defect?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significant CKD confirmed; nephron reserve critically reduced; transplant planning may be needed

questions.question: Is annualized eGFR decline >3 mL/min/1.73m²/year confirmed on ≥3 serial measurements?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — progressive CKD trajectory; secondary FSGS typically progresses more slowly than primary if cause controlled; rate >3 indicates inadequate cause management

questions.question: Is there significant tubular atrophy or interstitial fibrosis (>25% of cortex) on renal biopsy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — chronic irreversible nephron loss confirmed; limits benefit from cause control interventions

questions.question: Is >30% of glomeruli globally sclerosed on biopsy, reflecting advanced adaptive glomerulosclerosis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — extensive glomerular dropout; functional nephron mass critically reduced; aggressive cause control and BP management required

questions.question: Is BP persistently ≥140/90 mmHg despite ≥3 antihypertensive agents including RAS blockade?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — uncontrolled hypertension; major CKD progression accelerator; target <130/80 mmHg per KDIGO

questions.question: Is there coexisting metabolic syndrome (diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance) amplifying hyperfiltration injury?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — metabolic syndrome confirmed; multiple hyperfiltration drivers present; SGLT-2 inhibitor addresses both CKD and metabolic risk
